tasks.title: B18 Fix the Study create-to-list flake in the new browser job
tasks.description: CI run 35501617040 (the first real browser job run, added by B16) failed at scripts/test-ui-features.mjs:546 with 'created Study chapter did not appear in the list' although POST /api/study returned 201. Root cause was client-side stale-response ordering, not a server bug: src/ui-study.js mount() AND show() each call loadChapters(), so the first #/study navigation fired two concurrent cookie-less list GETs (the server mints a fresh study_player cookie per request in routes-study.js viewerOf, line 80); the create handler's non-awaited, unguarded refresh could be clobbered by those slow stale empty responses resolving afterwards (rows 1 -> 0). Fix: (1) optimistically insert the returned res.chapter into state.chapters and re-render, (2) a monotonic listSeq guard that discards any superseded response, (3) a listPromise that de-dupes the mount()/show() double GET so first contact mints ONE guest identity. Harden the browser assertion: replace the fixed 700 ms sleep + one-shot count with a bounded 5 s / 50 ms waitForFunction keyed on the created title (still requires the real row), plus bounded waits for the viewer panel and the server-validated quiz reply. Reproduced deterministically with a Playwright route.fulfill probe holding the two first-contact list responses 2.5 s: old code rows=0 text='No chapters yet.', fixed code rows=1 throughout; reverting only ui-study.js via git stash restores rows=0. Full npm run test:browser passed 3x under the CI env block. Guard: the browser step is the coverage; server identity scoping is already covered by test/study-chapters-selftest.js (17/17). Reproduce locally: HANDOVER.md section 18.

tasks.title: B19 Fix the seat-badge flake in the new browser job
tasks.description: CI run 35504521830 (the fix/study-create-flake push) had every non-browser job green but the browser job failed fast (30 s) at scripts/test-ui-features.mjs:145 with 'Expected seat badge to show Playing White, got: Seated: Black'. Root cause is the same class as B18: a fixed sleep racing an async round-trip, not a seat-auth bug. The step selects bot colour white (human takes black; badge 'Seated: Black'), then selects black (human must take white). The bot-select change handler calls sendBotConfigUpdate(), serialised on botConfigChain (src/ui.js), which POSTs /api/bot then awaits leaveSeat() and claimSeat('white'); updateSeatUI (src/ui.js:2472-2492) writes 'Seated: White'/'Seated: Black'/'Unseated'. A fixed waitForTimeout(500) could read the stale 'Seated: Black' on a loaded runner. Fix: replace the sleep with a bounded waitForFunction polling #seat-badge for 'White' (5 s / 50 ms; the catch throws with the current badge text), and replace the waitForTimeout(600) after the #new-game click with a bounded wait on #command-status settling to data-state success/error on the 'Starting new game' label plus an explicit error throw. Mutation-proven (pointing the wait at a never-appearing string fails with the real badge text; repo untouched). Full npm run test:browser passed 9/9 isolated runs under the exact CI env block. Only scripts/test-ui-features.mjs changed. Follow-up: the stress found a SEPARATE pre-existing undo-request flake (fixed waitForTimeout(300) before e2e4 can 400 illegal-move; the top-level catch exits before serverProc.kill() so it leaks :39281) tracked by card fix-undo-browser-flake. Reproduce locally: HANDOVER.md section 19.

tasks.title: B20 Fix the undo-request browser flake and the spawned-server leak on failure
tasks.description: Two real defects in scripts/test-ui-features.mjs surfaced by the CI browser job. Defect 1: the G4 undo-request block awaits POST /api/reset inside page.evaluate (so the command IS applied) then waited a fixed 200 ms before claiming seats and sending e2e4/e7e5; the residual race is the page not yet having re-rendered the fresh position, so the room was still Black to move, e2e4 was illegal, the server answered 400 POST /api/move with 'error':'illegal move'/'moveStr':'e2e4', and the console-error gate (if consoleErrors.length > 0) throw) failed the whole run. A second fixed waitForTimeout(300) raced the same page state poll for the two moves. Defect 2: the top-level testUiFeatures().catch(err => process.exit(1)) exited BEFORE serverProc.kill(), leaking a node server.js holding :39281; the next run logged 'Server already running.' and cascaded. Fix: (1) after the reset, a Node-side bounded poll (for(;;) loop, Date.now()+5000 deadline, 50 ms page.waitForTimeout sleeps) that awaits a real page.evaluate(() => fetch('/api/state'+q, {cache:'no-store'}).then(r => r.ok ? r.json() : null).catch(() => null)) Promise and requires history.length===0 && board.turn==='white' && gameOver!==true, throwing a descriptive error with the last snapshot on deadline; this deliberately replaced page.waitForFunction(async () => ...) because Playwright does not await an async predicate (a returned Promise is always truthy), so that round-1 shape resolved on the first poll and gated nothing; (2) after the two token moves, a bounded waitForFunction(() => window.getLivePly() === 2, timeout 5000 polling 50) whose catch throws with the real ply, keeping the authoritative !==2 assertion; (3) serverProc and browser hoisted to module scope with a shared idempotent teardown() (SIGTERM the server, await browser.close(), each try/catch) called on both the success and failure paths before process.exit(0|1). No assertion weakened: the block still requires 2 plies before the request, 2 after decline, and exactly 1 after accept. Gate mutation-proven on a /tmp copy: changing the reset predicate to an impossible board.turn==='black' now FAILS at the reset wait with the descriptive error (exit 1), whereas the identical mutation exited 0 under the round-1 async waitForFunction (fail-open contrast). Leak mutation-proven on a /tmp copy with a deliberate early throw: the spawned server is reaped and :39281 is free (exit 1). Full npm run test:browser passes repeatedly under the exact CI env block on fresh mktemp -d dirs. Only scripts/test-ui-features.mjs changed. Reproduce locally: HANDOVER.md section 20.

tasks.title: B21 Fix the bot-config race that left the human on the wrong seat under load
tasks.description: The CI browser job failed at scripts/test-ui-features.mjs:150 with 'Seat badge never showed Playing White (got: Seated: Black)' holding for the full 5 s bounded wait, so it was not slowness. Reproduced locally with CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate rate=15 on a Playwright probe running the exact gesture (level 4 -> colour white -> level 7 -> colour black -> toggle on): the server ended with the bot on white and the human on black. Captured POST /api/bot bodies showed repeated stale writes. Two compounding defects in src/ui.js. Defect 1: sendBotConfigUpdateNow() re-read the live DOM (colorSelect.value / levelSelect.value / toggle.checked) at execution time, but it is queued on botConfigChain, so by the time an earlier call ran the DOM already held a newer selection; it POSTed the stale colour and then claimed the wrong human seat via humanColor = color === 'black' ? 'white' : 'black'. Defect 2: updateBotUI(data) wrote every /api/bot response back into the form fields, guarded only by document.activeElement !== field, so a slow response for an older request clobbered the newer selection. This is a real product bug (a user quickly changing bot colour/level on a slow connection ends up on the wrong seat), not a test flake. Fix: (1) sendBotConfigUpdate() now reads the DOM once, synchronously, at gesture time and passes an immutable snapshot into the queued sendBotConfigUpdateNow(snapshot), which never re-reads the DOM; (2) updateBotUI takes {applyControls=false} and does NOT write user-editable fields from a response by default - the DOM is the source of truth for the controls, while the bot.status badge and seat state stay server-authoritative; fetchBotConfig() passes applyControls:true (guarded by botControlsTouched) so initial page load still populates the controls. The leaveSeat() -> claimSeat(humanColor) serialisation is unchanged. Gate-4 clean (no makeMove/createInitialBoard/historyToSan), no inline handlers. Evidence: throttled exact-gesture probe at rates 10/15/20/30, 3 runs each, all PASS after the fix (Seated: White / botColor black); original failed 17/20 runs. Isolation probes: a latency-injected 2400 ms fidelity probe proves the four POST /api/bot bodies now exactly match the four gestures (original sent black/black/black/black); a 600 ms route-delay guard probe proves a slow older response no longer clobbers the newer DOM selection (original domColor clobbered to white; mutB reverting only the guard also clobbers). Because the two defects partially mask each other in the bare badge probe, each defect is proven load-bearing by its dedicated probe rather than the badge probe alone. Full npm run test:browser under the exact CI env block passed twice (exit 0, both sentinels, 'Seat badge in bot mode: Seated: White'); gates t0-deadcode 27/0, wave3-hygiene 87, reachability 49/49 KNOWN_DARK 10, about 12, lint 0, test:unit exit 0 with 0 FAIL. Only src/ui.js changed. Reproduce locally: HANDOVER.md section 21.

tasks.title: B22 Fix the History-scrub browser flake where jumpToPly raced the client state sync
tasks.description: The History-Scrubbing block of scripts/test-ui-features.mjs ends an otherwise-passing run intermittently on CI: Testing History Scrubbing DOM Reconcile & Ghost Piece prevention is reached, then the ghost assertion throws (Ghost white queen remained on d1 after jumping to ply 10). Root cause is the same class as B18/B19/B20, a fixed sleep racing an async client round-trip, NOT a rendering or referee bug. The ten plies are sent by awaited direct fetch('/api/move') calls, so each command is applied server-side before the loop advances, but the PAGE is a separate consumer: it mirrors the referee through SSE plus the pollReferee state poll (src/ui.js), and its liveHistory (read by getLivePly(), src/ui.js:827, exported at src/ui.js:3685) is only as current as the last state it received. The old fixed await page.waitForTimeout(300) is a bet that ten SSE/poll updates arrive within 300 ms; on a loaded runner they do not. jumpToPly(10) then clamps its target to liveHistory.length, so a short history means the scrubber never advances past the live board (white queen still on d1), and the ghost assertion (ghostCheck.d1 !== null) fires. Fix: replace the sleep with a bounded synchronous page.waitForFunction(n => window.getLivePly() === n, expectedPly, { timeout: 5000, polling: 50 }) where const expectedPly = testMoves.length; its .catch evaluates window.getLivePly() and throws 'Expected ${expectedPly} plies before history scrubbing, got ${ply}' (falling back to '(unavailable)' if the evaluate itself fails). The predicate is deliberately synchronous because Playwright does not await an async predicate (a returned Promise is always truthy), the same fail-open shape B20 called out. No assertion was weakened; the unrelated fixed sleeps in the file (the waitForTimeout(50) between moves, the 200 after the reset, the 150/200 around the two jumpToPly calls, and every sleep outside this block) were left untouched per scope. Evidence: mutation proof on a temp copy of the script (wait target forced to 999) fails the scrub step with 'Expected 999 plies before history scrubbing, got 10', exit 1, while the repo file still reads testMoves.length; full npm run test:browser under the exact CI env block (all CHESS_* state in a fresh mktemp -d, CHESS_PORT=39281, CHESS_RATE_LIMIT=100000) passed TWICE on fresh temp dirs, both exit 0 printing the scrub PASS line, SMOKE TEST PASSED and ALL UI & AI FEATURE TESTS PASSED SUCCESSFULLY with ZERO ERRORS, with :39281 free after each; gates t0-deadcode 27/0, wave3-hygiene 87, reachability 49/49 (KNOWN_DARK 10), about 12, npm run lint 0. Only scripts/test-ui-features.mjs changed. Reproduce locally: HANDOVER.md section 22.

tasks.title: B23 Fix the History-scrub seat race where a stale browser-side premove re-claimed the seat
tasks.description: After B22 the History-Scrubbing block of scripts/test-ui-features.mjs was still intermittently red on CI. It sent the ten plies with TOKEN-LESS POST /api/move calls after a fixed waitForTimeout(200); /api/reset does NOT release seats (only the GC collector collectRoom() calls seatAuthManager.resetSeats, server.js:422), so a seat claimed by an earlier gesture survived the reset and the moves 401ed (validateMove, src/seat-auth.js:146). The deeper, previously-unseen cause was a stale browser-side premove. The earlier move-review section's #e2 -> #e4 click leaves e2e4 in premoveQueue (src/ui.js:51) because it is not White's turn and those squares are not a legal White move at that instant; renderBoard's premove flush (src/ui.js:1361-1393) then fires submitMoveToReferee('e2e4') when the fresh post-reset state arrives, and submitMoveToReferee AUTO-CLAIMS the seat (src/ui.js:798-800) - so the page re-took White out from under the test's out-of-band claims (intermittent 409 Seat 'white' is currently occupied), landed a stray ply (observed history [e2e4], turn black, whiteOccupied true), and /api/state never showed a fresh 0-ply board.
